gloss: warding off misfortune; protective charm against bad luck

definitions.gloss: warding off misfortune; protection against bad luck; (good-luck) charm
definitions.explanation: The act of warding off misfortune, calamity, or bad luck through prayer, ritual, or a protective charm — a central concept in Japanese folk belief and at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples. Also used as an attributive noun for items or rituals that serve this purpose, such as {厄除|やくよ}けのお{守|まも}り (a protective amulet).

examples.japanese: {厄除|やくよ}けのお{守|まも}りを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a protective amulet to ward off bad luck.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{厄除|やくよ}けのお{祓|はら}いを{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I received a purification ritual for warding off misfortune at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {厄年|やくどし}には{厄除|やくよ}けのために{寺|てら}や{神社|じんじゃ}にお{参|まい}りする{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: During one's unlucky year, many people visit temples and shrines to ward off misfortune.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}は{毎年|まいとし}{初詣|はつもうで}で{厄除|やくよ}けのお{守|まも}りを{新|あたら}しくして、{古|ふる}いものは{神社|じんじゃ}に{返|かえ}すようにしている。
examples.english: Every year at the New Year's shrine visit, my mother replaces her protective amulet with a new one and returns the old one to the shrine.

notes:
Composed of {厄|やく} (misfortune, calamity) and {除|よ}け (warding off, keeping away — from {除|よ}ける). {厄除|やくよ}け refers both to the abstract idea of warding off bad luck and, attributively, to items or rituals that do so.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{厄除|やくよ}け is closely tied to the concept of {厄年|やくどし} — "unlucky years" at certain ages (traditionally 25, 42, and 61 for men, 19, 33, and 37 for women, counted in {数|かぞ}え{年|どし}). During one's {厄年|やくどし}, it is customary to visit a shrine or temple for a {厄除|やくよ}けのお{祓|はら}い (purification ritual) or a {厄除|やくよ}け{祈祷|きとう} (prayer). Protective amulets called {厄除|やくよ}けのお{守|まも}り are sold at shrines and temples year-round but are especially popular at New Year's.

USAGE:
Often used attributively before another noun: {厄除|やくよ}けのお{守|まも}り (protective amulet), {厄除|やくよ}け{祈願|きがん} (prayer for protection), {厄除|やくよ}けの{神社|じんじゃ} (shrine famous for warding off misfortune). Can also be used as a standalone noun: {厄除|やくよ}けに{行|い}く (to go for a misfortune-warding ritual).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厄除|やくよ}けのお{守|まも}り: amulet for warding off bad luck
- {厄除|やくよ}け{祈願|きがん}: prayer for protection from misfortune
- {厄除|やくよ}けに{行|い}く: to go (to a shrine/temple) for a protection ritual
- {厄除|やくよ}けの{神社|じんじゃ} / お{寺|てら}: shrine / temple known for warding off misfortune

RELATED TERMS:
- {厄年|やくどし}: unlucky year — a traditionally inauspicious year of one's life
- {厄払|やくばら}い: exorcism of bad luck — a purification ritual, close in meaning
- お{祓|はら}い: Shinto purification ritual
- お{守|まも}り: (protective) amulet — general term
- {祈祷|きとう}: prayer, invocation (at a shrine or temple)
